(a) CMDPs are a useful model for learning from side information in healthcare applications, (b) we propose algorithms that learn efficiently in this setting under a smoothness assumption, (c) we give a tractable linear CMDP setting that allows us to give a KWIK learning algorithm, and (d) we give PAC lower bounds for CMDPs that are polynomial in the number of episodes and the context dimension, but exponential in the MDP dimension.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
(1) we introduce CMDPs and show that they are PAC learnable; (2) we propose a KWIK learning algorithm for CMDPs in the linear case; (3) we provide a PAC bound for CMDPs in a general setting.

we provide a general framework for learning in a class of CMDPs, and give a tractable algorithm for a subclass of CMDPs that is based on the KWIK framework.
The main takeaway from our work is that
smoothness of the MDP parameters with respect to the side information can lead to provably efficient algorithms in CMDP settings.
in the linear setting, the sample complexity of learning CMDPs scales polynomially with the dimension of the context, whereas in the general setting the dependence on the dimension is exponential.
the smoothness assumption is a useful way to characterize the amount of information provided by the context, and that the linear model is a tractable setting in which to apply this assumption.
